Lina (AE): Quick ask: prospect needs our CAIQ export + a one-page shared-responsibility blurb focusing on KMS behavior (rotation, revocation, residency) for a 2-week POC. They also want a Dedicated vs hosted-with-CMK price and a short runbook to demo key revocation. Can someone take point?

Harper (Sec): I can own CAIQ + SR blurb. Two clarifying q's: 1) EU-only keys or EU-primary with failover allowed? 2) Do they want us to run the revocation step during the POC (requires a customer admin to revoke grants)?

Diego (SE): From the kick-off: EU-primary, failover to US permitted only if keys are replicated in their KMS. They want a live revocation demo. Traffic est ~5 rps, tests include 8k token generation. Prefer Dedicated for audit, open to hosted-with-CMK if cost savings are large.

caiq-bot: CAIQ template (internal): https://redwood.internal/security/ca iq/ca iq-2026-template (latest export available)

Harper (Sec): Draft shared-responsibility bullets (plain language):
- Redwood: runs the inference servers, manages host patching/OS updates, encrypts platform data at rest (AES-256), and enforces TLS in transit.
- Customer: controls the data they send to Redwood, manages application secrets (API keys), and controls KMS key material if CMK is used (including rotation and revocation).
- CMK nuance: When customer-managed keys are used, Redwood performs cryptographic operations using grants/roles; we never persist plaintext key material. If the customer revokes grants, decryption fails and calls will return clear crypto errors until grants are restored.

Diego (SE): For the runbook I'll include steps for Dedicated (VPC peering + KMS grant) and hosted-with-CMK (IAM role + audit export). Example IAM snippet and smoke test to include.

Example IAM policy (to paste into customer's KMS):
```
{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [
    {
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Principal": {"AWS": "arn:aws:iam::REDWOOD_ACCOUNT:role/redwood-kms-access"},
      "Action": ["kms:Encrypt","kms:Decrypt","kms:GenerateDataKey"],
      "Resource": "arn:aws:kms:eu-west-1:123456789012:key/EXAMPLE-KEY"
    }
  ]
}
```

Smoke test (example):
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDFWD_KEY" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -d '{"input":"smoke test","max_tokens":2000}'
```
Expect success before revocation; after customer revokes the grant expect a 4xx DecryptError and matching KMS audit event. We'll capture timestamps and audit log entries as evidence.

Sam (Pricing): Rough cost sketches (ballpark):
- Dedicated POC (1x A10G-equivalent pool reserved for 14 days + private networking + storage + egress + setup): ~USD 16,500. Includes a small burst buffer and 48-72h setup.
- Hosted-with-CMK (shared pool + CMK integration + logs export): ~USD 2,700 for 14 days.
- Optional: live revocation demo with on-call engineer support during customer test window: one-time ops fee USD 1,500.
I'll break these into line items (GPU hours, storage GB, egress GB, ops hours) and post a sheet.

Lina (AE): Perfect. Owners: Harper = CAIQ export + annotated R/Y/G flags + SR blurb; Diego = runbook + IAM snippet + revocation checklist; Sam = itemized quote spreadsheet. Tell customer 48h turnaround for docs, 72h if they want the live revocation demo scheduled.

Harper (Sec): Will export CAIQ with flags and short rationales. I'll call out key residency (AMBER) and host-access notes for hosted plans (AMBER). ETA EOD.

Diego (SE): Runbook draft by 3pm: VPC peering steps, IAM grant JSON, smoke test commands, revocation verification checklist. I'll also add curl examples and a sample log query to show KMS audit events.

Sam (Pricing): I'll upload itemized quote at 4pm and link it here.

Lina (AE): Thanks team f44d I'll update the prospect and hold scheduling until we confirm runbook availability.
